clue.text: Germs mostly returned? One's sick, on reflection

indicators.note: mostly means the word for returned loses its final letter here

parts.note: someone returned is back
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: on reflection means the word for sick is mirrored, read from right to left

parts.note: sick means ill

explanation.surface: A wry aside about germs turning up again and someone feeling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Germs mostly' looks like a single phrase, but 'Germs' alone is the definition and 'mostly' works on the next word; 'on reflection' turns only the word for sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria, a kind of microbe that causes disease.

clue.text: A difficult problem for fellows caught in farm equipment

indicators.note: caught in means the fellows are trapped inside the machine

parts.note: a baler is a farm machine that packs hay into bales
F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Two men get trapped in a farm machine, a tricky situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A baffler is a puzzle that confounds or perplexes.

clue.text: Gave cash for party activity and went on a group rave?

explanation.surface: Friends chip in for a party, then go out dancing together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubbed together' is an idiom for pooling money; the second sense reads it as went clubbing as a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooling funds is the idiomatic sense; going to nightclubs en masse is the literal one.

clue.text: Dismal day upset servant

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into another order

explanation.surface: A gloomy day leaves a servant upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges DISMAL and DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady's maid is a female domestic attendant to a lady.

clue.text: Being dragged within capital of Wales

parts.note: into can mean inside or within

indicators.note: capital of means take the capital, the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone is hauled into Cardiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of' looks like a pointer to Cardiff but asks for W, Wales's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being towed or pulled along is said to be in tow.

clue.text: Vehicle completely overturned, carrying one ice-cream ingredient

indicators.note: carrying means the van and its companion hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: overturned means the word for completely is turned the other way round

parts.note: completely means all, as in all done
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An ice-cream van has tipped over with one tub of flavouring inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice-cream' tempts you towards a van selling it; the vehicle is just VAN, and 'carrying' places the Roman one between it and the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is the flavouring pod used in classic ice-cream.

clue.text: Not lively, but moving in a wild way

indicators.note: moving means the letters shift into another order

explanation.surface: Something sluggish yet stirring wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges NOT LIVELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Violently means with savage force, in an unrestrained manner.

clue.text: Some infection (as always) in the nose

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cold, as usual, settles in the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose.

clue.text: Artist — divine and cool RA at work

indicators.note: at work means the letters are busy rearranging themselves

explanation.surface: A Royal Academician is busy creating something divine and cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' rearranges DIVINE AND COOL RA; RA (Royal Academician) looks like a painter, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Like unpaid jobs woman avoided for ever

indicators.note: avoided means the woman abbreviation is left out of the word

parts.note: unpaid jobs earn no wage, so they are wageless
W is the abbreviation for woman, as on forms

explanation.surface: A woman steers clear of unpaid work for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoided' drops W from WAGELESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageless means eternal, never growing old, lasting forever.

clue.text: Mood supplied by cosmetics is something to build on

indicators.note: supplied by means the mood piece follows and is provided by the cosmetics piece

parts.note: foundations are make-up bases, a kind of cosmetic
a tone is a mood or atmosphere

explanation.surface: Wearing make-up lifts your mood and gives you a base for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious break after the tenth letter misleads: the cosmetics are plural, and the mood word takes only the last four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundation stone is the first block laid at a building's base, literally a starting point for construction.

clue.text: See! Cream reduced parts of ears

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: reduced means the word for cream is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: the cream of something is the best

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch cream being boiled down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts BEST to BES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobes are the soft fleshy lower parts of the ear.

clue.text: Width and height seeable, possibly — this is indicative of a car's length

definitions.text: this is indicative of a car's length

indicators.note: possibly means these letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Measurements of a car you can see might tell you how long it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges H and SEEABLE after the width letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelbase is the distance between front and rear axles, which tracks a vehicle's overall size.

clue.text: Seaside resort's favourite display of luxury

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire, England
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A holiday town's best-loved attraction is a lavish show.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside town on England's north-east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out a crimson carpet is the ceremonial welcome given to VIPs, a sign of lavish treatment.

clue.text: China's obscure railway lines are studied in this

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
to mist is to obscure or cloud

explanation.surface: A Chinese railway is hidden by fog, its lines under study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate). 'lines' looks like railway track but means the creases on a palm.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmistry is fortune-telling by reading the creases on the hand.

clue.text: The Underworld -a dark area, first to last

indicators.note: first to last means the opening letter is shifted to the end of the word

parts.note: a shade is a shadowy dark area

explanation.surface: A description of the underworld as a gloomy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the S of SHADE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the Greek realm of the dead, the classical underworld.

clue.text: Excitement from shade with a shriek

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
and means along with
a cry is a shriek

explanation.surface: Someone gets agitated by a colour and screams.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue and cry is a public outcry or commotion.

clue.text: Supporting United, and dead boastful!

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A fan brags about backing United to the death.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean arrogant or vain, full of self-praise.

clue.text: Sun almost ruined after unrealistic hope

indicators.note: after means the ruined piece comes behind the hope piece
unrealistic means the letters are not true to their form, so rearranged
almost means the word for ruined loses its final letter

parts.note: bust means broken or ruined

explanation.surface: A dreamer's hopes collapse under the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unrealistic' makes PHOE from HOPE; 'almost' cuts BUST to BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebus is a name for Apollo as god of the sun, used poetically for the sun itself.

clue.text: Bet browser is a churchman

parts.note: to lay a bet is to wager
someone who browses books is a reader

explanation.surface: A gambler and a bookshop browser turn out to be a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay reader is a non-ordained person licensed to lead parts of church services.

clue.text: Pauses to hold one's checks

indicators.note: to hold means the word for pauses contains the next piece

parts.note: rests are pauses
one's is I's, read as I plus S, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone stops to keep their cheques safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is I + 'S, giving IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back, to fight against it.

clue.text: Finished run in this crumpled garment

parts.note: something finished is over

indicators.note: in means the run letter goes inside the word this
crumpled means the letters are crushed into a new order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: After a run, someone's shirt is creased and done for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside THIS; 'crumpled' rearranges those letters into SHIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: An overshirt is a loose shirt worn over other clothes as a light jacket.

clue.text: Burn to chant end of tune

parts.note: to chant is to sing

indicators.note: end of means take the last letter of tune

explanation.surface: A singer is told to burn the final note.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to scorch slightly.

clue.text: Finish off with item of menswear more expensive

parts.note: a tie is worn by men
prices that are up are higher

explanation.surface: Ending a shopping trip with a pricier tie.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie up loose ends is to complete or settle them.

clue.text: Exploding stars, never huge, tail off

parts.note: no can mean never, as in no way

indicators.note: tail off means the word for huge loses its last letter

parts.note: vast means huge

explanation.surface: Big stars blow up and then fade away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail off' cuts VAST to VAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares to great brightness through an explosion.

clue.text: Causing some disgraceful behaviour out of the pub-lie eye?

explanation.surface: Drunken trouble breaks out away from a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase as being behind, i.e. responsible for, the scenes (public rows) that someone makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who causes rows is the cause of scenes; anything done privately happens away from view, both senses of the phrase.

clue.text: Unhappy about church's uncanny ability

indicators.note: about means the word for unhappy goes round the church abbreviation

parts.note: sorry means sad or unhappy
CE is the abbreviation for Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable about a church's strange powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is witchcraft, the use of magic powers.

clue.text: Measurement of acidity cissy dodged in Science

parts.note: pH is the scale measuring acidity

indicators.note: dodged means the letters jink about into another order

explanation.surface: A timid boy skips the acid tests in science class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodged' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters of the timid word jink about. 'in' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics is the branch of natural science dealing with matter and energy.
